title: Min Stack
description:
Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element, each in constant time.

Implement the MinStack class:

  • MinStack() initializes an empty stack.
  • void push(int val) pushes val onto the stack.
  • void pop() removes the element on the top of the stack.
  • int top() returns the element on the top of the stack.
  • int getMin() returns the smallest element currently in the stack.

You are graded on a recorded sequence of calls. The first entry names the class and its constructor arguments; every entry after that names a method and its arguments. Methods that return nothing report null, and so does the constructor.

Constraints:

  • -2^31 <= val <= 2^31 - 1.
  • pop, top and getMin are only ever called on a non-empty stack.
  • At most 3 * 10^4 calls are made in total.
  • Every operation must run in O(1) time, so rescanning the stack to find the minimum does not qualify.

exampleTestCases.explanation: getMin reports -3 while it is on the stack. After the pop, the top is 0 and the smallest remaining value is -2.
Pushing 1 lowers the minimum to 1; popping it restores the previous minimum of 2.
Duplicates are independent entries, so the stack still holds a 5 under the one on top.

testCases.explanation: The worked example from the description.
The minimum falls and then recovers as the smaller value is popped.
Equal values must each be tracked separately.
A single element is both the top and the minimum.
The minimum rises again once the smallest value is removed.
Popping one of two equal values leaves the other as top and minimum.
Negative duplicates: removing the smallest restores the earlier minimum.
A value pushed after the minimum does not change it, and popping both restores the original.
Two copies of the minimum: removing one keeps the minimum at 0.
Extremes of the allowed range, ending with a push that becomes the new minimum.
